messages.content: Write a post about why a company is investing in developer relations. Around 250 words.

output:
**Why we're hiring for developer relations**

We shipped a good API in March and watched it go nowhere for four months.

Not because it was broken. The docs were accurate, the SDK worked, the pricing page said what it meant. But everyone who tried to build with it hit the same wall around hour two — auth scoping, which our reference documented in a way that made sense only if you'd already written the code. Twelve support tickets. All of them the same ticket.

We can keep answering that ticket one person at a time. Or we can hire someone whose whole job is to catch it before the twelfth person files it.

That's the bet. Developer relations, done properly, isn't marketing in a hoodie. It's a feedback loop with a person in the middle: someone who builds real things on our platform, feels the friction firsthand, and has enough standing inside the company to make engineering care.

So the role reports to product, not marketing. The metric isn't impressions or conference talks. It's time-to-first-successful-call, currently 51 minutes, which we want under ten by spring. Plus two others we'll publish quarterly: docs PRs merged, and how many rough edges arrive as filed bugs rather than as tweets.

We'll get parts of this wrong. Every DevRel team drifts toward whatever is easiest to count, and we probably will too for a stretch before we notice.

The posting is live. Come tell us what we're missing.

~250 words. The specifics — March, twelve tickets, 51 minutes — are placeholders; swap in your real numbers, since they're carrying most of the credibility here.
